exposure: mode of birth in previous term-born pregnancy
emergency caesarean birth at full dilatation
outcome: Medically indicated preterm birth at less than 37 weeks of gestation
cohort: 16,340 women with first two consecutive singleton births and the first birth at term
finding: Compared with vaginal birth, emergency caesarean birth at full dilatation was associated with an increase in spontaneous preterm birth, while elective caesarean, emergency caesarean at <4 cm dilatation, and emergency caesarean at 4-9 cm dilatation were associated with increased medically indicated preterm birth.
mod_finding: Term caesarean in the first stage of labour or performed prelabour is associated with medically indicated preterm birth, while term caesarean in the second stage of labour is associated with spontaneous preterm birth.
